practiceDecisions.assessment: Requires failed/cancelled result, no runner/steps and explicit acquisition annotation; only newest same-workflow/branch/event run, at most three attempts. Runtime and Formal AI comparison remain pending.

practiceDecisions.assessment: Digest verification belongs to the download action; the extractor rejects traversal, symlinks and collisions and streams bytes. No hosted archive extraction executed in this batch.

Dependency graph reports unavailable/unknown on PR and fails with an action on main. Broken live links remain failures despite archive availability. Source review is not live API verification.

practiceDecisions.practice: Independent warning, secrets, docs and workflow-tool checks
practiceDecisions.assessment: Pinned lint tools, actual warnings and checked Git inventories are separate gates. Remaining transitive scripts, runtime execution and Formal AI counterparts need complete review.

practiceDecisions.practice: The execution budget remains active after its root exits
practiceDecisions.assessment: The pinned template checks its root status file before group liveness, returning success with a live finite child. The actual Formal AI production wrapper independently returns 0 in 0.07s while its child keeps stdout open for four seconds under a one-second budget. A local repair retains group liveness after root exit and passes seven finite process controls; upstream repair and exact-head hosted validation remain pending.

practiceDecisions.practice: Complete security findings and release credential preflight evidence
practiceDecisions.assessment: The six complete pinned helper/test sources are read. The template SARIF helper checks every recursively discovered nonsymlink report, findings and extraction notifications. Formal AI currently invokes CodeQL analysis without this explicit result gate. The template probes crates publish authorization without a tarball while stating that ownership still needs real publication; Formal AI records the token as unknown. Both registry preflights open a session but ignore cancellation failures. Cargo own-manifest warnings need a separate check from rustc deny-warnings. Applicable adoption, runtime regressions and hosted proof remain unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Release helper I/O, heading boundaries, package identity and pinned tool dependencies
practiceDecisions.assessment: The twelve complete pinned sources are read. The template propagates output writes and changelog directory/entry/read errors, and skips fenced release headings while preserving body bytes. Formal AI get-version warns and succeeds on output failure; get-bump-type drops directory-entry/read failures and suppresses output failures. Those applicable differences remain to implement and verify. Both version bump helpers still use a whole-manifest version regex; dependency-first manifests are an unexecuted source question. Template parser and scanner manifests use explicit versions plus lockfiles; actual Formal AI equivalents need a full closure decision. Git configuration propagates errors in both repositories.

practiceDecisions.practice: Pinned development inputs, lint configuration and example boundaries
practiceDecisions.assessment: Read all base configuration, manifest, license and small example/test sources. Formal AI already separates test targets, forbids unsafe code, applies the same Clippy families and commits the binary lockfile. Its resource-conscious profiles intentionally differ. Template exact tool pins, archive closure, link policy and source/header preservation require remaining workflow and dependency closure verification. Example sum application is domain-specific and is not a replacement for Formal AI behavior.

practiceDecisions.practice: Parsed version identity and branch authorization
practiceDecisions.assessment: Template check-version-modification parses package/workspace version identity and never grants a release exemption from an untrusted branch name. The fully read Formal AI counterpart still uses a whole-document version regex and grants four release-prefix exemptions. Its head-versus-current-base comparison deliberately handles merged base versions and moved manifests and must be preserved when repairing identity and authorization. Applicable repairs and native behavioral verification remain unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Release registry uncertainty and fallible outputs
practiceDecisions.assessment: Template check-release-needed delegates registry operations to a module and propagates errors. The fully read Formal AI counterpart treats transport/status/parse problems as missing artifacts and warns then succeeds on output write failure. Its separate immutable all-target recovery observer refuses unqualified publication and must remain intact. Applicable ordinary-path registry/output repairs are pending; no delivery credit is inferred from source inspection.

Template check-cargo-lock resolves selected package identity from Cargo metadata and requires a binary lockfile to exist in the HEAD commit. Formal AI has no same-named helper, while its dependency audit enumerates tracked locks and Rust CI uses locked inputs. A full equivalent-behavior decision remains unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Registry uncertainty, crate publication and package path helpers
practiceDecisions.assessment: Fully read the four complete pinned helpers. Registry metadata parsing, bounded HTTP requests and distinctions between absence and transient/permanent failures are applicable comparison inputs. Sparse visibility currently trusts successful API status without identity proof; package identity uses a table-local regex rather than full TOML. Rate-limit publication deferral, Cargo credential-store fallback and dependent-job ownership need actual Formal AI workflow/counterpart comparison and executable evidence. No implementation or upstream-repair credit is established by this read.
